author: Russell Brand
description:
Four companies produce roughly 90 percent of all the meat consumed in the United States — one of them Brazilian — and every one of them is ultimately owned not by farmers but by investment conglomerates including Blackrock, Blackstone, and Vanguard. Russell Brand and TJ break down how American ranch hands sign contracts with these giants and walk away with between $25,000 and $35,000 a year while oligarchs quietly buy up vast tracts of agricultural land across the country. The communal franchise farming model they propose is not just an alternative business structure but a direct challenge to the stranglehold that Big Food and its financial backers have over the entire food chain, and the people at the top of that chain are not going to give it up without a fight.

author: Russell Brand
description:
It started with Australia building internment camps during Covid — something Russell says has been quietly ushered to the edges of collective memory. Then Canada froze the bank accounts of ordinary citizens who donated to trucker protesters and called them Nazis. Now the UK is piloting a digital ID system that Russell argues was never about online safety but about building a vast AI-monitored database linking every click, every comment, and every search directly to an identifiable person so the government can preemptively act against political dissidents before they become a problem. This is not a conspiracy theory. This is the plot of Minority Report and it is happening right now.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand sat across from Nigel Farage on Question Time and called him a pound shop Enoch Powell to his face, arguing that framing migrants as the primary cause of a country's decline was not politics but the calculated stirring of hatred and disdain. Years later Russell says something has shifted — that when he actually engages with people who hold nationalist views he finds not hatred but a genuine attempt to protect tradition, land, culture, and rights that are being eroded from the top down. The question he keeps returning to is how people at the bottom of a culture with no institutional power can possibly be held responsible for the direction that culture is heading.

author: Russell Brand
description:
In this Sunday Service with The Brands Laura talks about rest and how noticing, receiving and praise provide a basis for connecting with God and others. A white feather (pictured) drifts into the space and provokes a conversation about loved ones that have passed and superstorm versus intuitive noticing of relational grace. Plus it’s Laura’s birthday. Happy Birthday Laura Brand.
